Gadi Eisenkot says national unity must rest on shared values. To explore them with Likud, he sent Netanyahu’s former chief of staff to meet Netanyahu’s former personal lawyer.

Yoav Horowitz and Chili Tropper represented Eisenkot’s Yashar party, and Ofir Katz and Michael Rabello represented Likud, when the talks opened Sunday at Herzliya’s Dan Accadia Hotel. Naftali Bennett also sent a representative.

Yashar says it is offering a government led by Eisenkot and denies reports of a proposed premiership rotation. Its conditions include universal military or civilian service and acceptance of Israel’s Declaration of Independence.

The talks also let Eisenkot show that he tried unity before turning to other coalition options. Likud, meanwhile, has a seat at negotiations over replacing its own leader.
